name: asgi.py
summary: Django ASGI configuration file that exposes the ASGI application entry point for the conversationalBI project.
purpose: This element exists to bootstrap Django in an asynchronous server context and expose the standard ASGI callable. It solves the deployment problem of connecting the conversationalBI project to ASGI-compatible servers (e.g., Uvicorn, Daphne, Hypercorn) to handle concurrent and async protocols such as HTTP/2, WebSockets, and long-polling.
responsibilities: Initialize Django for asynchronous request handling
Expose the ASGI application callable as the module-level variable named application
Act as the standardized entry point for ASGI web servers
inputs: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment variable (or its default value)
outputs: ASGI application callable (application) consumed by ASGI servers
architecture_notes: This file serves as a minimal bootstrap adapter following Django conventions and the 12-Factor App methodology. It isolates deployment infrastructure concerns from domain logic by residing in the project-level config package. The use of django.core.asgi.get_asgi_application() delegates protocol handling to the framework, avoiding custom middleware logic at the entry point and ensuring vendor-neutral compatibility with any ASGI server. For future async expansion (e.g., Django Channels, WebSockets), this file would become the integration point for custom routing or protocol-type routers.
improvements: Add explicit try/except and structured logging around application initialization to surface startup failures clearly
Add type hints (e.g., ASGIApp) to the application variable for better static analysis and IDE support
If async features or WebSockets are planned, integrate a protocol-type router (e.g., Django Channels) here instead of the default synchronous-only application
Wrap the application with observability middleware (request ID, tracing, or metrics) at the ASGI level for cross-cutting concerns
Add a startup validation check to confirm critical settings are loaded before the server accepts traffic
